column1: # D6's pass conditions for HR-23's stage 2 (brief P4-4-HR23; brief P4-4-HR2325S, deliverable 1), written before the counted run and before any rehearsal on these cases, from the brief and docs/phase4/D4-hr23-design.md alone. Restated on 2026-11-16 from the design at #715's head 41de13af, rules (A) and (B') (D1's 6907176282 and 6907928324; D4-112 item 5), by a D6 instance that read no stage-3 code, rehearsal or result: no expectation of C2's here comes from a run. D3's M2 (mal-midflow) was added on 2026-11-16 from the design on main at b3156950, sections 2.3 and 4.7 (D4-113 item 3.1), by another D6 instance that read no stage-3 code and took no expectation from a run. mal-bprime's TCP clause was restated on 2026-11-17 from design section 2.3's measured TCP statements on main at c991f096 (#739; D4-116 item 6, D4-117 item 2), by a D6 instance that wrote none of #739: its svc=removed over TCP rests on 2.3's measured stops under C0 and C1p, and its exception on 2.3's third measured statement, which sets no expectation but ?.

# This file decides, with hr23-cases.tsv and hr23-malformed.tsv. Each row cites the design section it rests on; tests/fixtures/network/gt-pcap/hr23/SOURCE.md and fp/SOURCE.md say how the captures are made.
# op and value are a row's threshold, where it has one. Any edit changes this file's SHA-256: test_hr23_conditions.py pins it.

column5: rule
C0: Zeek as on main, the zeek/zeek image at pins.env's ZEEK_IMAGE, with today's script (design 4.1). D4-100 item 2's control, and what every c0 cell pins.
C1: the same binary as C0, with the script with part (a) (design 3, 4.1). Part (a)'s effect is judged as C1 against C0.

C1p: the project's build from option (i)'s pinned inputs without the patch, with the script with part (a) (design 4.1). Part (b)'s effect is judged as C2 against C1p. A row on which C1p differs from C1 shows the build, not the patch.
C2: the option (i) build named by its image digest and the tarball's and the patch's SHA-256s (design 4.5), with the script with part (a). The engine that ships; a rebuild is not this configuration.

C0, C1, C1p and C2 run in one run, on the same captures and the same runner image. A result from another run is not carried over. Stock Zeek and ICSNPP are shown beside C0 and are not judged for the fix (design 4.2).

The run prints likely_server_ports under each configuration (ports.zeek). The pins assume C0's set as run 43373373987 printed it (hr23_cases.LIKELY). A case or rerun flow whose ports fall on the other side of a configuration's set, so that the sides it gets differ from the label's side column or from sides.tsv, reads unknown under that configuration, never pass or fail.

Labels come from how each capture was built (hr23_cases.py, fp_set.py, dnp3_cases.py), never from an engine. A forged DIR takes its label from the builder's role (design 4, opening). tshark's reading is reported beside them, and every difference is in hr23/tshark-beside-labels.tsv or fp/tshark-beside-fp.tsv with its cause; it is never used as a label.

Each row of hr23-cases.tsv is judged by rules 1 to 9 of docs/phase4/D6-engine-run-pass-conditions.md section 1, rule 6 included, under each configuration on its own. Under C0 a Service row is read from conn.log's responder; under C1, C1p and C2 from the script's link rows (design 3 item 7). An objects row is the Objects reading of the function row with the same columns (rule 9's object matching).

pass, fail and present are the expected result. A cell fail (<reason>) expects a result that starts with fail, and the run's reason is reported beside it. A row or configuration that did not run is unknown, never pass.

a: part (a)'s fix shows on the row when C1 and C1p show their pinned pass and C0 its pinned fail. b: part (b)'s fix shows when C2 shows its pinned pass and C0, C1 and C1p their pinned fail. unknown: C0 passes the row, so it reads unknown for the fix whatever C2 shows, never pass (brief P4-4-HR23, stage 2). premise: dnp3-udp-master-short; if any of its rows fails under C0, option (i)'s premise does not hold and the choice goes back to the comments before stage 3 (design 4.1). control: the row is a control (judge-swap, judge-link). r1: R-1's attacker-caused second server (design 3 item 4, section 6), reported against its pin and never a pass.

A row whose c2 cell is pass and that C2 fails is a regression: of the patch where C1p passes it, of the build where C1p fails it too. A row whose c1 cell is pass and that C1 fails is a regression of part (a).

column2: a control that does not do what is pinned
column5: If C0, C1 or C1p does not show its pinned cell on a row, the row reads unknown for the fix, and stage 3's acceptance test, that the control does what stage 2 pinned row by row, fails on it. It is a finding, never a pin edit (brief P4-4-HR2325S, risks).

An objects row whose fix is b reads unknown for the fix when, under C0, the objects row of the same objects fails on the case that is its control: dnp3-udp-swap-control for g34v1; dnp3-udp-master-short for g60v1, g60v2, g60v3, g60v4, g80v1 and g50v1; dnp3-udp-dir-spoof for g12v1. A C0 pass there shows that Zeek's request parser reads those objects at all, so that C2's pass is the fix's.

The control of section 1 item 2's swap at creation. If C0 fails any of its rows, the swap is not what the design reads, and every relay-started UDP case reads unknown for the fix under every configuration.

present: a link row of the script's with is_orig true, stamped with the time of packet 3 (C, the master's first frame), which only PIA_TCP::ReplayStreamBuffer can write, since no frame of the outstation's carries that time (design 4.1, D6's N-A). If it is absent under C1, C1's pass on the case's Service row reads unknown: the master's DIR-set frames may have passed it alone.

The harness reports, under C1, C1p and C2, every flow whose link rows name both ends (design 3 item 4). Among the cases it is expected on dnp3-udp-dir-spoof and dnp3-tcp-dir-spoof only. Anywhere else among the cases it is a finding against this pin.
Each capture of hr23-cases.tsv and hr23-malformed.tsv, and each class of the false-positive set, is read by its own Zeek process, so that one input's failure or crash reaches no other.

A run counts only from main, with hr23-cases.tsv, hr23-malformed.tsv and this file at the SHA-256s that test_hr23_conditions.py holds, and every capture at the builders' committed hashes (hr23/hr23.sha256, fp/fp.sha256, dnp3/dnp3.sha256). D4 adds the SHA-256s of hr23-cases.tsv, hr23-malformed.tsv and hr23-conditions.tsv to pins.env with stage 3's build; D6 does not edit pins.env, except a hash update of those three lines that D1 authorizes. Any other run is a rehearsal.

Run under C0, C1, C1p and C2 (design 4.3). Each input is judged on every token of its c0 cell under C0, C1 and C1p, and of its c2 cell under C2, read as mal-states says. A token that does not hold fails that input under that configuration, and is a finding, never a pin edit.

Under every configuration: no crash, and no reporter error but the one an input's cell names (err=target, on dnp3-mal-udp-len-1 to -3, design 4.3). Any other is a finding: against the patch when C1p does not show it; in Zeek or the build when C1p or C0 shows it too, and then never netted out, and it goes by the disclosure rule of design 4.6 (design 4.3).

<msg>=seen: a function row of that message's code from its sender on the input's flow, with every object the builder's label names for it (rules 2, 7 and 9). <msg>=code: that function row, with none of its objects (design 1 item 5: the code is read and the objects are not). <msg>=absent: no function row of that message's code from its sender beyond those of other messages. The messages are those the build cell names.

C2 equals C1p on the input: every weird by name and count, the violations, the reporter errors, every function, objects and link row of the flow, and the count reqhdr reads (mal-reqhdr). A difference is a regression (design 4.7, what (i) does not change), except the link rows that mal-link names.

The input has a fragment on design 2.3's list of where C2's parser differs from C1p's: a code of 129 to 131 with 4 or more application octets from the originator; any other code from the responder, at any length; a code of 129 to 131 with 2 or 3 octets from the responder (rule (A)'s cost); and 0 or 1 octets from the responder, which mal-unknown judges. C2 is judged on its c2 cell: the binpac result C1p gives the same bytes from the side whose parser rule (A) picks, the responder's for 129 to 131 with 4 or more octets and the originator's for every other fragment (the twin rule, design 4.7), so below 4 octets every code's twin is the originator's. Weirds and reporter errors stay those of the input's own side, and the record of a throw is mal-bprime's. hr23-malformed.tsv's judge column is twin exactly on the inputs with such a fragment and no mal-unknown ground, and test_hr23_conditions.py derives it from the builder's units.

column2: the three states of a stop
column5: Each cell reads as one of three states, which the judge scores from the logs of the input's flow (D1's 6907928324, condition 2). Parsed on: viol=0, and every message the cell names after X =seen or =code. Recorded stop: viol=1, exactly one analyzer.log row on the flow, under the DNP3 analyzer, and every message the cell names after the stop =absent; with svc=removed where the cell names it. Silent stop: viol=0, no reporter.log row, every message the cell names after the stop =absent, and svc=dnp3: no record at all, as the stock build's stop on a UDP flow's first datagram left none (design 2.3, its measured statement, run 43772135241, CI-Linux, simulated). A stop that a weird or a reporter error records is scored on its weird= and err= tokens. The fourth: an analyzer.log row on the input's flow under any analyzer but DNP3_UDP or DNP3_TCP (PIA_UDP among them) fails the input under that configuration whatever its cell says, and is a finding, never a pass. svc= reads conn.log's service for the flow: dnp3 when it holds dnp3_udp or dnp3_tcp, removed when it holds neither. Each state is defined here so that the judge can be tested on constructed logs for each.

From design 2.3's (B') and 4.7's What (B') changes, and no expectation of C2's here comes from a run (D4-112 item 5): a throw in a datagram that the PIA replays, the first of a flow that starts with DNP3, is a silent stop under C0, C1 and C1p and a recorded stop under C2, one DNP3 violation with svc=removed below 10 KiB; a throw on any later UDP datagram is a recorded stop under all four, with the same failure_reason text; over TCP a throw is a recorded stop under all four, the replayed segments included, since PIA_TCP::ReplayStreamBuffer calls NextStream inside its catch and (B') does not touch TCP, with svc=removed below 10 KiB, as each of design 2.3's measured TCP stops shows under C0 and C1p (rehearsal 44104409796, CI-Linux, simulated), C1 and C2 desk. Over TCP there is one exception, from 2.3's third measured statement, which sets no expectation: a throw in the connection's first data, on a connection to a port in likely_server_ports: where it was measured, it raised a second DNP3_TCP violation with the first's failure_reason, stamped at the other end's next data frame, and whether either end's later messages were parsed is unknown. Such an input's viol, and every message its cells name after the throw, are ?; this takes precedence over mal-midflow's recorded stop under C2. It was measured on 20000 alone, with two inputs, one from each end, and 20000 is both in likely_server_ports and DNP3_TCP's registered port, at which the analyzer attaches at the connection's start; which of the two gives the shape is unknown, as is its cause, so the clause reads ? on every port of the set as a precaution. On a connection to 20001, in the first measured statement's order (X, then the same end's message), a throw in the first data is a clean recorded stop (2.3's first measured statement); the exception's order there, the other end's message next, was not measured. dnp3-mal-udp-fc129-badobj-first and its TCP twin are inputs on which C2's parser throws where C1p's parses on (design 4.7, Both directions), as the flow's first data; the twin's connection is to 20001, so the exception does not reach it, and no input of the malformed set has the exception's shape, which test_hr23_conditions.py finds from the builder's units; mal-midflow's two are such inputs in mid-flow.

D3's M2 on #718 (D4-113 item 3.1; D1's 6910729374), from design 4.7's Both directions and 2.3, never from a run: the two inputs on which C2's parser throws where C1p's parses on, each one datagram in mid-flow on a flow M5 starts, between P R and Q R. dnp3-mal-udp-fc129-badobj-mid, from the originator: M5's 129 of 5 application octets, IIN then one object octet, -badobj-first's X; C1p's request parser takes it by its default arm, and C2's response parser rejects the cut object header. dnp3-mal-udp-fc1-badobj-mid, from the responder: O1's read (code 1) of 4 application octets, an object type and no qualifier; C1p's response parser takes it, by its 4-octet header and its Debug_Byte arm, and C2's request parser throws in Request_Objects, since 2 octets are short of Object_Header's first two fields (3). Each reads parsed on under C0, C1 and C1p and a recorded stop under C2 (mal-states), a throw on a later UDP datagram (mal-bprime). test_hr23_conditions.py finds from the builder's units every input with such a fragment, the -badobj-first pair among them, checks that each reads so, and that those in mid-flow include one from each side. Such a fragment is on design 2.3's list, is taken by C1p's parser whatever its octets (the originator's 129 to 131 by the request parser's default arm, the responder's other codes of 4 or more octets by Debug_Byte), and leaves C2's parser, by rule (A), 1 or 2 octets of an object header: after the 4-octet response header for 129 and 130, after the 2-octet request header for 1, 2 and 5 (design 4.7's twin rule).

reqhdr=<n>: the count of application headers with code 129 to 131 raised as a request header (dnp3_application_request_header) on the input's flow, from either side, as the harness reports it (design 4.4, D6's N9 on #715). Under C0, C1 and C1p a 129 to 131 is a request header exactly from the originator; under C2 exactly when it has fewer than 4 application octets (rule (A)). Every input whose X carries 129 to 131 names it, so that (A)'s edges, exactly 4 octets and 131, show where viol and Q cannot: a bound of more than 4, or a rule without 131, changes reqhdr on those inputs (D3's M3 on #718). test_hr23_conditions.py derives each value from the builder's units.

The input's result rests on generated code that the patch rewrites (design 4.7 items 1 and 2: link lengths 4 and 6, 0 or 1 application octets, a fragment of more than one frame, a header held at the connection's end). C2 against C1p is measured and reported beside its c2 cell, not judged; a crash or an unexpected reporter error still fails it.

column2: link rows of a held header
column5: On dnp3-mal-udp-len-0 to -4, -chunk-crc, -nofir, -nofin-fir and -limit, and the four dnp3-mal-tcp-eof- inputs, whether a link row is written for a header that binpac holds when its fragment then fails is generated code (design 4.1, 4.7 item 1). Their link rows are reported, not judged, under C1, C1p and C2.
On dnp3-mal-udp-dir-both and -dir-change, part (a) names both ends under C1, C1p and C2 (design 3 item 4). The both-ends field is expected there, and reported.

test_hr23_builder.py checks from the bytes: that dnp3-mal-udp-octets-2's and -3's octets, with Q's first octets, make a header whose CRC fails, so that their viol=1 is the header CRC's; each input's link length, transport octet and application octets as its name says; every 129 to 131 input's code and length; and that each -badobj-first input's X is its 5-tuple's first data, 5 application octets with IIN and one object octet, followed by P R and Q R whole; and that each -badobj-mid input's X is one datagram between P R and Q R, all whole, on a flow M5 starts, from the end and with the octets mal-midflow names, its DIR its role's. test_hr23_conditions.py derives from the builder's units each input's judge (mal-twin), its reqhdr under each configuration (mal-reqhdr), and whether any frame's DIR disagrees with its side, which every such input's cells name as weird=dnp3_unexpected_flow_direction (design 1 item 4).

The malformed set and the HR-23 cases are fuzz seeds (resync-conditions.tsv's fuzz-seeds and fuzz-bit7). None holds a TCP hole, so no FuzzBuffer chunk of theirs sets bit 7. dnp3-mal-udp-limit does not fit fuzz-max-len and is listed as not converted.

fp_set.py, built once for HR-23 and HR-25 (D4-111 item 5.2): classes (1) to (5) of design 4.3 over UDP, and class (6) over TCP as resync-conditions.tsv's fp- rows name it, each item on its own 5-tuple and each class one capture. HR-23's run reads every class under C0, C1, C1p and C2.

HR-23 sets the floors that HR-25's rows set, so neither run's is larger: (1), (2), (4) and (5) at least 300 items each, (4) at least 75 of each protocol; (3a), (3b-data), (3b-link) and (3c) at least 30 each; (6) at least 100 without a hole and 30 with one. As built: 306, 300, 304 and 304; 32, 42, 32 and 54; 104 and 32. test_hr23_builder.py checks the counts.

Exact for every class: no datagram, and for class (6) no end's stream and no run of it between holes, holds 05 64 with a passing header CRC at an offset its class does not name (fp_set.passing_headers; HR-25's fp-redraw). A class (4) item draws again by its flags or its authenticator.
Named flows under C0, C1, C1p and C2, under both readings (conn.log's service, and a link row), per class. Zero in 300 bounds the rate at about 1% per flow at 95% (rule of three), per class.

Named under C0 by conn.log: its header CRC confirms the flow, and its chunk CRC raises only a weird and skip (design 4.3). Under C1, C1p and C2 the link-row reading is unknown (design 4.1): measured and reported.

Named under every configuration, by both readings, C0 included: a false positive, recorded under HR-23 (3c) and R-1, not closed (design 4.3). Each item is sent from the originator with a code other than 129 to 131 (arm-3bdata), so C2's parser is C1p's, off design 2.3's list, and C2 equals C1p on it (design 4.7).
Named under C0 by conn.log from its second datagram on; never under C1, C1p or C2 by the link-row reading, which no link-only frame writes (design 3 item 6, 4.3).

Under C0, C1 and C1p one violation per item, and named by conn.log only until it: dpd.zeek removes the service (design 4.3). Each item is sent from the originator with a code other than 129 to 131, so C2's parser is C1p's and C2 equals C1p on it, its violation included (design 4.7). Its link-row reading is unknown (design 4.1).
Named flows under C0, C1, C1p and C2, under both readings: no header of class (6) passes its CRC, so nothing confirms a flow.

Per class and reading, every flow that C2 names C1p names too: part (b) must not turn an unnamed flow into a named one (design 4.3). A flow named by C2 alone is a false positive of the fix, and fails.
Per class and configuration, the flows with a flow record that are named under neither reading, beside C0's count (design 4.3). Reported, not judged.
Per class and configuration: the class's size, the flows named under each reading, the violations, and the dnp3_ weirds by name. Never netted out against a control.

Every row of engine-pass-conditions.tsv at its pin; every GT-PCAP DNP3 capture (dnp3/dnp3.sha256); the PRP pairs (prp-pairs.pcap and prp-derived.sha256); the public captures (MANIFEST.tsv, extra-captures.tsv); E2's corpus rows (modbus-signature-conditions.tsv at its pin); and HR-24's stage 3 once it is pinned (design 4.3). Under C0, C1p and C2, with C1 beside.
A row of a rerun's own conditions that C0 passes and C2 fails. C1p then says whether the build or the patch caused it (design 4.3).

column2: the sort of every rerun flow
column5: hr23/sides.tsv: for each flow of each capture on which the pinned tshark reassembles a DNP3 application fragment, the side Zeek gives each end and how many fragments C2's parser takes otherwise than C1p's, by hr23_tshark.py sides (design 2.3's list; 4.7, where it shows): C2 takes the response parser exactly for 4 or more application octets with code 129 to 131 (rule (A)), C1p exactly for the responder's, each fragment's octets from tshark's reassembled length. It covers the GT-PCAP DNP3 captures, the PRP pairs, the public DNP3 captures and their PRP pairs, and the HR-23 cases. E2's corpus and HR-24's stage 3 are sorted in the run by the same pinned tool. The run checks each flow's orig against C1p's conn.log; a flow on which they differ reads unknown.

column2: a flow with no changed fragment
column5: C2's parser agrees with C1p's on every fragment, so C2 equals C1p on the flow: every Protocol, Service, Function, Objects and group 120 verdict, every link and fc row of the probe, the weirds and the violations (design 4.7, the last bullet of what (i) does not change). A difference is a regression, except on rerun-multiframe's fragments.

column2: a flow with any changed fragment
column5: C2's parser disagrees with C1p's on at least one fragment. Judged by the twin rule where its rows are pinned: dnp3-udp-temp-port's responses' flow, whose two responses reach the response parser under C2 with its rows unchanged (design 4.7), and dnp3-udp-unsolicited's flow (hr23-cases.tsv). Elsewhere C2 against C1p is reported, with a crash or a reporter error still a finding.

column2: fragments of more than one frame
column5: Every fragment of more than one frame, in any rerun capture, is in design 4.7 item 2's list: expected equal to C1p's, and reported as unknown, not as a regression.
C2 against C1 and C1p, which run the same script, emits no record or field that the script does not emit now (D4-100 item 2; design 4.3). Against C0, part (a)'s DIR field is the one new field.

For each capture and configuration (design 4.4): weird.log's count of dnp3_unexpected_flow_direction and of every other dnp3_ weird by name; analyzer.log's rows, read for failure_reason and the analyzer's name only; the count of frames whose DIR disagrees with their code's class; the count of application headers with code 129 to 131 raised as a request header (mal-reqhdr); the both-ends field; both named readings; and the SHA-256 of the zeek binary in the image. The judge reads these only as judge-both and the mal- and fp- rows say.
The harness reads no payload: not analyzer.log's failure_data, not a weird's addl beyond its name (design 4.4).
tests/integration/gt_pcap/hr23-cases.tsv, hr23-malformed.tsv and hr23-conditions.tsv, pinned by test_hr23_conditions.py.

hr23_cases.py and fp_set.py write every capture frame by frame with dnp3.py and synth.py. tests/fixtures/network/gt-pcap/hr23/ and fp/ hold their SHA-256s, labels, tshark's expected differences and the sort; the hr23 job of a6-gt-pcap.yml rebuilds them and checks all four, and the prp job checks the public captures' sort. The captures are never committed.
